newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator asks Treasury review cap gains rules.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator asks Treasury review cap gains rules.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Tom Harkin asked the Treasury Department Monday to review loopholes in tax laws that he said allow the very wealthy to avoid paying the full 28 percent capital gains tax on stock profits.
"There are cases where individuals have reportedly avoided millions in taxes in a single year -- meaning larger deficits and higher taxes for average taxpayers," the Iowa Democrat said.
Harkin cited three mechanisms used to avoid paying tax on gains, including placing shares in a charitable trust, which then gives them back to the individual in a way that avoids capital gains tax.

In a second method used to avoid capital gains taxes, an investor, rather than selling stock, would borrow identical stock from a brokerage firm and sell that. The firm would receive a fee for loaning the stock and the investor's original stock would serve as collateral for payment.
In a third method, an investor would sell a note with the rights to the stock, effectively the same as selling the stock but without triggering the capital gains tax.

"There are legitimate public purposes for waiving capital gain taxes, such as genuine charitable donations or the legitimate passing of company ownership to employees," Harkin said. He called on the Internal Revenue Service to investigate and fine those who abuse the system.
